intro: Missing the court date on a traffic ticket creates a second Class C charge — failure to appear, or violate promise to appear — stacked on top of the original citation. Attorney Robert Navar resolves both cases together, working to keep either one from becoming a conviction.
summaryHeading: One missed court date, two cases: how failure to appear works in El Paso
summary: Failure to appear (FTA, often listed as VPTA) is a separate Class C misdemeanor under the Texas Transportation Code, filed by the court when you miss the appearance date on a citation. You now have two cases, not one.
An FTA charge generally comes with an arrest warrant and can lead to an OMNI report to DPS that blocks your license renewal until the court clears it.
We handle both cases together: ask the court to recall the warrant, then work toward a dismissal or deferred disposition on the original ticket and on the FTA where the court allows it.

Common defenses include never receiving notice, a wrong address on the citation, or a court error. Our flat fee is $59 per ticket in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 in JP and area city courts, plus $35 for the first warrant.

sections.heading: The Promise You Signed on the Citation
paragraphs: When an El Paso officer hands you a citation, you sign a written promise to appear in court by a certain date. The Texas Transportation Code makes breaking that promise its own offense — a Class C misdemeanor the dockets call failure to appear or "violate promise to appear" (VPTA). It carries its own fine and court costs, set by the court, and it is filed whether the original ticket was for speeding, no insurance or an expired registration.

One ticket becomes two cases with two cause numbers. In El Paso Municipal Court they appear separately on the warrant list, each with its own fine and often its own warrant. Three violations at one stop and a missed date can mean six cases.
Many clients learn about the FTA months or years later — at a license renewal, on a background check, or when a routine stop on I-10 ends in an arrest. Neither the charge nor the warrant expires.

sections.heading: What Follows an FTA: the Warrant and the License Hold
paragraphs: Two things happen behind the scenes once an FTA is filed. First, the judge signs a warrant on the original ticket and often a second warrant on the FTA charge. Second, the court can report you to the Texas Department of Public Safety under the Failure to Appear program in Transportation Code Chapter 706 — the OMNI hold. DPS will not renew your driver's license until the court sends a clearance, and the court collects a program fee on each reported case before the clearance goes out.

This is why an FTA is worse than the ticket. The ticket was a fine. The FTA adds a second fine, a warrant, a license hold, and the cost of untangling it. The good news is that the same attorney appearance that gets the warrant recalled also puts the FTA on a pretrial docket where it can be negotiated like any other Class C case.

sections.heading: Resolving the Ticket and the FTA on One Docket
paragraphs: Once you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance on every open cause number — the ticket and the FTA — and request that each warrant be recalled. Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised. The court then resets everything to a pretrial setting where Robert Navar meets with the prosecutor.

Our request on the FTA charge is a dismissal, and El Paso prosecutors are often willing to consider that when the underlying ticket is being resolved and the client has no pattern of missed dates. On the original citation we pursue the same outcomes we pursue on any ticket: a dismissal, deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45A.302 (formerly art. 45.051), or, where the judge allows it, a driving safety course dismissal. No result can be promised in advance.
You generally do not attend the pretrial. For many clients, our first call after hiring is to say the warrants are gone, and the second is to say how both cases ended.

sections.heading: Notice Problems and Other Defenses We Look For
paragraphs: Failure to appear is not automatic just because a date passed. The offense under Transportation Code §543.009 requires proof that the driver "wilfully" violated the written promise to appear, and in El Paso we see the same fact patterns that undercut that element: the citation listed an old address, the court mailed a reset notice that never arrived, the officer wrote an appearance date that fell on a weekend or court holiday, or the client was deployed from Fort Bliss, hospitalized, or in custody elsewhere on the date.

Court error happens too: a payment posted to the wrong cause number, a lost defensive-driving request, a case reopened for a missing certificate. When we pull the court's file we are looking for exactly these gaps, and when we find one we present it to the prosecutor as the reason the FTA should be dismissed outright rather than deferred.

Even without a clean defense, the FTA is a fine-only Class C case. Judges and prosecutors tend to care more about resolving the underlying ticket than punishing a missed date, which gives an attorney room to negotiate.

sections.heading: FTA Practice Outside El Paso Municipal Court
paragraphs: The statute is the same across El Paso County, but the practice differs. The Justice of the Peace precincts handle FTAs on Sheriff's, constable and DPS trooper tickets; Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton each have their own judge, docket day and habits about dismissing FTAs. Our flat fee there is $69 per ticket, plus the $35 / $20 warrant add-on.

Because an FTA in one court can sit beside an older one in another, we start with a county-wide check. Our free ticket and warrant lookup finds each open case and tells you the court, the charges and the total fee before you pay anything. Se habla español.

sections.heading: Two Things Not to Do, and What to Send the Office
paragraphs: Do not pay the ticket online to make it go away. Paying enters a plea and a conviction on your DPS record, and it may not clear the separate FTA case or the OMNI hold. Do not go to the courthouse window without a lawyer; an active warrant can be served there.
Call us or submit the lookup form, and send what you have. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

faqs.q: Is failure to appear a criminal charge in Texas?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the Transportation Code it is a Class C misdemeanor, the same level as the traffic ticket itself. It is fine-only, but it is a separate case with its own cause number, its own fine and, in many cases, its own warrant.

faqs.q: If I pay the original ticket, does the failure to appear charge go away?
faqs.a: Generally not. The FTA is its own case and must be resolved separately. Paying the ticket also enters a conviction on your record, which is the opposite of what we want. Let us handle both cases together on one docket.

faqs.q: Can a failure to appear be dismissed?
faqs.a: Sometimes. El Paso prosecutors are often willing to dismiss the FTA when the underlying ticket is being resolved through dismissal or deferred disposition, and particularly when there is a notice problem such as a wrong address. We ask for that dismissal on every FTA we handle, but no outcome can be promised.

faqs.q: Will a failure to appear show up on a background check?
faqs.a: An open FTA with a warrant can appear on some background checks and can block your license renewal through OMNI. Once dismissed, or dismissed after a completed deferral, the case may be eligible for expunction under the Code of Criminal Procedure's expunction chapter.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to fix a failure to appear in El Paso?
faqs.a: Our fee is $59 per ticket in El Paso Municipal Court or $69 in JP and area city courts, plus $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one. Court fines and costs, if any, are set by the court and depend on the outcome. Consultations are free.

faqs.q: I never got a court date. Do I still have an FTA?
faqs.a: Possibly. Courts file FTAs based on the date on the citation, not on whether you received a reminder. If the citation had a wrong address or the date was never communicated, that is a real defense, and we raise it. Start with the free lookup so we can see what the court filed.
